answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to stake a meaningful, time-locked deposit before it can earn, with reputation that accrues slowly over a long horizon rather than instantly. An opal-like identity layer, one verified credential per real operator rather than per wallet, makes creating hollow armies of sock-puppet agents expensive, because each fake identity must lock fresh capital and build history from zero. Sybils stay unprofitable when the cost of entry exceeds the reward.
